narrative.overview:
AgonProject is a research tool, so it should look like one: a clean notebook on the desk of an argumentation researcher. The page is pale, cool paper. The argument graph is the drawing on it. The brand blue is the pen, used to mark what matters (the selected option, the primary action, the menu entry you're about to pick) and almost nowhere else. Panels, toolbars and windows are ruled margins that frame the work and never compete with it.

Density is moderate. The editor is a working surface that people stay in for a long session, so chrome is compact (small buttons, 14px UI text, hairline borders) but never cramped. Secondary pages (glossary, generator, attributions) feel like notebook pages: a ruled header bar, then content. The serif display face appears only for the AgonProject wordmark, like a title written on the notebook's cover.

Colors, fonts and radii are each defined in exactly one place and consumed through tokens. Desktop and mobile are one system at two densities, not two designs.
keyCharacteristics: Cool blue-gray paper neutrals, one brand blue accent, a warm yellow used sparingly.
Inter for everything functional; Fraunces only for the wordmark; JetBrains Mono for formulas and code.
Hairline `base-300` rules separate regions; shadows only lift things that float over the canvas.
Two radii do almost all the work: field (8px) for controls, box (12px) for containers.
Same tokens, same components on desktop and mobile; mobile only changes density and touch size.

rules.name: The Single Source Rule
rules.body: No raw hex, `rgb()` or Tailwind primitive colors (`gray-500`, `text-black`) in app code. Every color comes from a palette token. Graph rendering, export output and the standalone maintenance page are the documented exceptions.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Muted text and icons use exactly three ink strengths over `base-content`: `/80` for secondary body text, `/65` for meta, captions, labels, placeholders, empty states and muted icons, `/40` only for disabled controls and decorative glyphs that carry no information. Full-strength ink is the default. No other steps, and no `opacity-*` to fake a tier.

rules.name: The Readable Floor Rule
rules.body: `/65` is the lightest ink for text anyone needs to read: it clears WCAG AA (4.5:1) on paper and paper shade in both modes, `/60` does not in light mode. Never set readable text at `/40`.

rules.name: The One Pen Rule
rules.body: Brand blue marks the one thing you're about to act on or have selected. If a screen has more than a handful of blue elements at rest, something is shouting.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: Desktop and mobile share the scale above. No arbitrary sizes (`text-[13px]`, `text-[0.8125rem]`); snap to the nearest step (11→12, 13→14, 15→16).

rules.name: The Cover Only Rule
rules.body: Fraunces is the notebook's cover. If it appears on anything that isn't the wordmark, it's wrong.

rules.name: The Shared Label Rule
rules.body: Small caps headings always come from `.section-label` or `.field-label`, always in ink, never in `primary` or `secondary`.

rules.name: The One Shell Rule
rules.body: Secondary pages never invent their own top-of-page structure. No floating back links above a big title, no margin-only layouts.

rules.name: The Same Bones Rule
rules.body: A desktop view and its mobile twin use the same components (header bar, search, tabs, labels). Mobile may stack, enlarge touch targets and reflow, but not restyle. The one sanctioned difference: page tabs become pills on compact screens (see Tabs).

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never use Tailwind's opacity modifier on shadows (`shadow-lg/30`). It generates a different class that skips the palette tint. Use the named tiers.

rules.name: The Float Only Rule
rules.body: Cards and panels sitting in the page flow get a hairline border, not a shadow.

dos: Do take every color from a palette token and every typeface from a font role.
Do use ink, ink `/80`, ink `/65` and (for disabled or decorative only) ink `/40`.
Do build every secondary page on the header bar shell.
Do use `.section-label` and `.field-label` for all small caps text.
Do separate in-flow regions with `base-300` hairlines and reserve shadows for floating surfaces.
Do reuse the same component on desktop and mobile and change only density.
donts: Don't use arbitrary font sizes (`text-[13px]`, `text-[0.6875rem]`); snap to the scale.
Don't use `shadow-*/NN` opacity modifiers; they skip the palette tint.
Don't use Fraunces anywhere but the wordmark.
Don't color caps labels with `text-secondary` or `text-primary`.
Don't mix back icons (`ArrowLeft`, `ArrowUturnLeft`) or invent new close-button sizes.
Don't fade icons with `opacity-*` to make them muted; use the ink tiers. Opacity is for disabled states only.
Don't add a third radius for controls (`rounded-lg`, `rounded-md`); use field or box.
